about: Phase 15 unit 7, the determinism suite (gate item 3). The runs the suite makes, and the tolerance each artefact is compared with. scripts/matrix/determinism.py runs and grades it; the 'Determinism' section of docs/developer/testing.rst states the same tolerance with its justification, and determinism.py check-doc is red when the two differ.

configurations.label: repeat-1
configurations.why: the pinned run: Comet with 4 threads (the matrix's setting), Percolator's defaults (seed 1, 3 threads)

configurations.label: repeat-2
configurations.why: the same run again, in a fresh project

configurations.label: comet-threads-1
configurations.why: Comet single-threaded: every protein searched by one thread in file order

configurations.label: comet-threads-0
configurations.why: Comet's own default, one thread per core (64 on the reference host)

configurations.label: percolator-threads-1
configurations.why: Percolator single-threaded: the folds trained one after another

configurations.label: percolator-threads-8
configurations.why: Percolator with more threads than folds

configurations.label: control-seed-2
configurations.why: another seed draws other folds: Percolator's results must change, Comet's must not

artefacts.why: each query is scored and its candidates ranked by one deterministic rule whatever thread scores which protein: a candidate's xcorr is summed by one thread and rounded to 3 decimals, the per-query histogram takes integer adds under the query's lock, a tie for the last stored place is broken by peptide string, candidates are sorted by xcorr then peptide then modification sites, queries by scan then charge before anything is written, the E-value is fitted per query, and no random number is drawn

percolatorThreads.name: order of rows tied on Percolator's sort keys
percolatorThreads.why: Percolator sorts its results with std::sort, which is not stable, on (score, scan, expMass, label); PSMs of one spectrum with identical features (positional isomers of an oxidised methionine, ranks of one scan) score exactly alike and stay unordered. Measured: at --num-threads 1 against 3 such rows change places, their values identical; repeats at one thread count never do. Rows are compared as a set only within a block of consecutive rows equal in score, q-value, PEP and scan number
percolatorThreads.source: Percolator rel-3-07-01 src/Scores.cpp:44-46 (operator> keys), :241-242 (postMergeStep: sort, greater<ScoreHolder>); ISO C++ [alg.sort]: std::sort is not stable
